mainTopic: Testing רבה's and רבא's reasons for בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם against three sources, and how רבה is defended each time
overview: Earlier, two reasons were given for why a שליח bringing a גט from overseas must say "בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם." רבה says it is because people there did not know a גט must be written לשמה. רבא says it is because no one there could confirm the signatures. The גמרא tests both reasons against three sources. The first source is about a שליח who could not say the declaration, which רב יוסף explains as a healthy שליח who became a חרש. The second is רב הונא's ruling that two people bringing a גט do not need to say it. The third is a תוספתא that calls the declaration a leniency for the woman. Each source fits רבא easily but seems hard for רבה. Each time, the גמרא defends רבה: the case is from after people learned the law of לשמה, a single שליח still speaks because of a גזירה, and rare cases are left out of the גזירה. Along the way it explains why a woman bringing her own גט must still declare (one rule for all שליחות) while a husband need not, since he will not challenge a גט he holds himself. For the תוספתא, the גמרא explains that the woman had already remarried.

steps.title: A deaf-mute cannot be an agent for a גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the "unable to say" שליח is a חרש, and then rejects this from a משנה that says a חרש cannot bring a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the agent who cannot speak is a deaf-mute, can a deaf-mute bring a גט at all? We learned in a משנה: everyone may bring a גט except a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to identify the שליח who is "unable to say" the declaration. Its first guess is a חרש, and it rejects that guess right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרש cannot speak, so he seems to fit "unable to say." But a משנה rules that a חרש may not serve as a שליח to bring a גט at all. So the earlier teaching cannot be talking about an ordinary חרש.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (the opening of a suggestion the גמרא is about to reject)
A deaf-mute, who in הלכה lacks legal competence
But we learned in a משנה (introduces a challenge from a משנה)
An imbecile, a person not mentally competent
A minor

phrases.english: If you say it means a deaf-mute,
phrases.notes: This is the agent the earlier teaching calls "unable to say" בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.

phrases.english: is a deaf-mute fit to bring a get?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִים לְהָבִיא אֶת הַגֵּט,
phrases.english: But we learned: Everyone is fit to bring a get,
phrases.notes: This משנה comes later in the מסכת, on דף כג.

phrases.english: except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor!

steps.triggerLanguage: אילימא חרש, חרש בר איתויי גיטא הוא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the analysis of the earlier teaching about an agent who is unable to say the declaration.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the "unable to say" agent is a חרש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה disqualifies a חרש from being a שליח for a גט, so he cannot be the case being discussed.

steps.title: רב יוסף: He became deaf after handing over the get
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the שליח was healthy when he gave the גט, and became a חרש before he could make the declaration.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The case is where he gave her the גט while he was healthy, but before he managed to say "It was written in my presence and signed in my presence," he became a deaf-mute.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the challenge by describing a special case. The שליח was a valid פקח when he carried out his job, and he only became a חרש afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says a חרש cannot serve as a שליח. Here the שליח was fully valid when he handed over the גט, so his job was done properly. He simply lost the ability to make the declaration before he said it.

keyTerms.meaning: With what are we dealing here? (introduces a narrowing of the case)
A person of sound mind, fully competent
It was written in my presence and signed in my presence (the declaration a שליח from overseas must make)
He became a deaf-mute

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where he gave it to her while he was competent,
but he did not manage to say
"It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence"
before he became a deaf-mute.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואמר רב יוסף הכא במאי עסקינן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The "unable to say" agent is an ordinary חרש, and a חרש is disqualified.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was a valid פקח when he delivered the גט and became a חרש only afterward.

steps.title: This fits רבא but is difficult for רבה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's case works well for רבא's reason, but it seems to contradict רבה's reason for the declaration.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבא this works well; according to רבה it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks רב יוסף's case against the two reasons given earlier for the declaration. It fits רבא, but it raises a problem for רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the declaration is about confirming the signatures, so if the signatures can be confirmed another way, the גט is fine. For רבה, the declaration testifies that the גט was written לשמה, and nothing else can replace that. So a גט without the declaration should not work, yet the teaching treats it as valid.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well
It is difficult
The אמורא who says the declaration is needed because of לשמה
The אמורא who says the declaration is needed because of confirming the signatures

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבה (with a ה) and רבא (with an א). They are two different אמוראים with two different reasons, and this whole sugya depends on telling them apart.

phrases.english: According to Rava it works well; according to Rabba it is difficult!
phrases.notes: This goes back to the two reasons given earlier: רבא's is about the signatures, and רבה's is about לשמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב יוסף's answer against the two earlier opinions.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reason, that the declaration is needed to testify about לשמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the declaration is needed for לשמה, a גט without it should not work. The teaching implies it does work, which fits only רבא's view.

steps.title: The case is after people learned the law
steps.stepSummary: To defend רבה, the גמרא sets the case in a later time, after people overseas learned that a גט must be written לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what are we dealing here? With a time after they learned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rescues רבה by moving the case to a later period. By then people knew about לשמה, so testimony about it is no longer really needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's concern was that people overseas did not know the law of לשמה. Once they learned it, that worry is gone. That explains why the גט can work even without the declaration.

keyTerms.meaning: After they learned (that a גט must be written לשמה)
For her sake; a גט must be written specifically for this woman

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
After they learned.
phrases.notes: Meaning after the people overseas learned that a גט must be written לשמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty against רבה from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the time period of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case comes from a time when people did not know about לשמה, so רבה would need the declaration.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case comes from after people learned, so the reason for the declaration no longer applies.

steps.title: Then even a healthy agent should not need to speak
steps.stepSummary: If people already know about לשמה, then even a שליח who can speak should not need to make the declaration.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even one who is able to speak should also not need to say it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of step 4. If everyone already knows, why should any שליח still have to say the declaration?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 removed רבה's reason for the declaration. But if the reason is gone, it should be gone for everyone, not only for the one who became a חרש. Confirming the signatures should be enough even for a healthy שליח.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge based on the previous answer)
One who is able (to say the declaration)
Also, too

phrases.english: If so, one who is able as well!
phrases.notes: Meaning that even a שליח who can speak should not need to say the declaration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 4 by extending its logic.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the case is after people learned about לשמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If knowing the law removes the need for the declaration, it should remove it for every שליח, including one who can speak.

steps.title: A decree so the old problem does not return
steps.stepSummary: Even after people learned, the Rabbis still required the declaration, so people would not forget and slip back into the old mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, lest the matter return to its corrupted state.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why a healthy שליח must still speak. The Rabbis made a גזירה to keep the old problem from coming back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strictly speaking, the declaration is not needed once people know about לשמה. But if the Rabbis dropped it, people might forget the law again over time. So they kept requiring it as a safeguard.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
Lest the matter return to its corrupted state

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest the matter return to its corrupted state.
phrases.notes: The worry is that people would forget again that a גט must be written לשמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once people learned the law, no שליח needs to make the declaration.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שליח who can speak must still make it, because of a גזירה to keep the old mistake from returning.

steps.title: Then the decree should apply to one who cannot speak
steps.stepSummary: If there is a גזירה requiring the declaration, then a שליח who cannot speak should also fail it, and his גט should not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then one who is unable should also be included!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the גזירה of step 6. If the Rabbis required the declaration, why does the גט work when the שליח cannot say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה normally applies across the board. So the Rabbis should also require the declaration from the one who became a חרש, and since he cannot say it, the גט should fail. That would bring back the original problem with the teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is unable (to say the declaration)

phrases.english: If so, one who is unable as well!
phrases.notes: Meaning the גזירה should cover him too, so his גט should not work without the declaration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the גזירה introduced in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה that the declaration must still be made.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the Rabbis required the declaration, the requirement should apply to the one who cannot speak too, which would invalidate his גט.

steps.title: The Rabbis did not decree on a rare case
steps.stepSummary: A healthy שליח who becomes a חרש is rare, and the Rabbis do not make גזירות about rare cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: A competent person who became a deaf-mute is an uncommon thing, and the Rabbis did not make a decree about an uncommon thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge and finishes defending רבה. The גזירה was never made for a rare case like this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rabbinic גזירות target situations that happen regularly. A שליח who becomes a חרש right after handing over the גט almost never happens, so the גזירה does not cover him. That is why his גט still works through confirming the signatures, even according to רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: An uncommon matter, something that rarely happens
The Rabbis did not make a decree about it

steps.whatToRemember: The "unable to say" שליח was healthy when he delivered the גט and only later became a חרש. For רבה, the case is from after people learned about לשמה. A healthy שליח must still speak because of a גזירה, but the Rabbis do not make גזירות for rare cases, so this rare case is left out of it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule "מילתא דלא שכיחא לא גזרו בה רבנן" is a general principle used throughout ש״ס to set limits on rabbinic decrees.

phrases.english: A competent person who became a deaf-mute is an uncommon matter,
and with an uncommon matter,
the Rabbis did not make a decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: פקח ונתחרש מילתא דלא שכיחא, ומילתא דלא שכיחא לא גזור בה רבנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 and closes the defense of רבה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limit on the reach of a rabbinic decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גזירה requiring the declaration applies to everyone, including one who became a חרש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה does not cover a rare case like a פקח who became a חרש, so his גט is valid even according to רבה.

steps.title: But a woman bringing her own גט is also rare
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that the Rabbis do not make rules for rare cases. A woman bringing her own גט is rare, yet the משנה still requires her to say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a woman bringing her own divorce document is also rare. Yet we learned in a משנה: the woman herself may bring her own גט, as long as she says 'It was written in front of me and signed in front of me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 8 by pointing to a rare case where the Rabbis still require the declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the Rabbis do not make rules for rare situations. A woman acting as the שליח for her own גט is also unusual. Even so, the משנה makes her say the declaration, so the 'rare case' rule seems not to hold.

keyTerms.meaning: Not common; a rare situation
We learned in a משנה
Brings her own גט
As long as; on condition that

phrases.english: But a woman [bringing her own גט], which is not common,
and we learned: the woman herself may bring her own גט,
as long as she is required to say
'It was written in front of me and signed in front of me'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'no rules for rare cases' answer of Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that the Rabbis do not make a גזירה for rare cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A woman bringing her own גט is rare, yet the משנה requires her to make the declaration

steps.title: So that people will not treat different kinds of שליחות differently
steps.stepSummary: The Rabbis made the woman say the declaration so that all kinds of שליחות would follow one rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that you will not make distinctions between different kinds of שליחות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the woman has to make the declaration so that every person who brings a גט follows the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her case is rare, so by the rule of step 8 the Rabbis would not have needed to include her. They included her anyway so that people would not start saying 'this שליח must declare and that one need not.' The פקח who became a חרש in step 8 is different: nothing required including his rare case, so he was simply left out of the גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: So that you will not make a distinction
Acting as an agent; bringing the גט for someone

phrases.english: So that you will not make distinctions in שליחות.
phrases.notes: He means: the Rabbis wanted every kind of agent bringing a גט, even the woman herself, to follow one rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a separate reason for including the woman: one uniform rule for all שליחות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since her case is rare, the requirement for her shows the Rabbis do make rules for rare cases
steps.terutzMaskana: She is included only so that the rule for all agents stays the same, not because of her own case

steps.title: Then the husband should also need the declaration
steps.stepSummary: If every kind of שליחות follows one rule, a husband who brings the גט himself should also need to say it. But a ברייתא says he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the husband should also have to say it! Why then does a ברייתא teach: if the husband himself brought his גט, he does not need to say 'It was written in front of me and signed in front of me'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 10 using the case of a husband who delivers the גט himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the goal is one rule for everyone who brings a גט, the husband should be included too. Yet a ברייתא clearly exempts him. So 'one rule for everyone' does not seem to be the real principle.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why then?
It was taught in a ברייתא
The husband

phrases.english: If so, the husband too [should have to say it]!

phrases.aramaic: אַלְּמָה תַּנְיָא: הוּא עַצְמוֹ שֶׁהֵבִיא גִּיטּוֹ,
phrases.english: Why then was it taught: he himself who brought his גט
is not required to say
'It was written in front of me and signed in front of me'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'no distinctions in שליחות' answer of Step 10
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If all agents are treated alike, the husband should also need the declaration, but a ברייתא exempts him

steps.title: A husband holding the גט will not challenge it
steps.stepSummary: The declaration exists to stop the husband from later challenging the גט. When the husband himself is holding the גט, that worry does not exist.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason the Rabbis said the declaration is needed? In case the husband comes, challenges the גט and makes it invalid. Here he is holding it in his own hand. Is he going to challenge it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the husband is exempt: the reason behind the declaration simply does not apply to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The declaration protects against a husband who later claims the גט is not valid. A husband delivering his own גט could just tear it up if he did not want the divorce, so there is nothing to protect against. The rule was never meant to cover him, which is different from a rare case or a case of keeping one rule for all.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Perhaps; in case
Challenges; contests the validity
Makes invalid
He holds it in his own hand

steps.whatToRemember: The woman must declare so that all agents follow one rule. The husband is exempt because the whole reason for the declaration, the fear that he will challenge the גט, does not exist when he is the one delivering it.

phrases.english: What is the reason the Rabbis said
he must say 'It was written in front of me and signed in front of me'?
Because perhaps the husband will come
and challenge it, making it invalid.
Now he is actually holding it in his own hand,
phrases.notes: If he did not want the divorce, he could just keep the גט or tear it up.

phrases.english: and he is going to challenge it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the reason for the rule does not apply to the husband
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Exempting the husband breaks the 'no distinctions in שליחות' principle
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband is not a case of the rule at all, since the fear that he will challenge the גט cannot exist when he delivers it himself

steps.title: שמואל asks רב הונא about two people who bring a גט from overseas
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new source. רב הונא rules that two people bringing a גט from overseas do not need the declaration, since two people would be believed even if they just said she was divorced in front of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: שמואל asked רב הונא, 'Two people brought a גט from overseas. Must they say "It was written in front of us and signed in front of us," or not?' He answered: 'They do not need to. After all, if they said "He divorced her in front of us," wouldn't they be believed?!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to use as proof in the discussion about the reason for the declaration. This step sets up the case, and the גמרא will draw its conclusion from it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's logic is that two people count as full witnesses. They are believed even to say outright that the woman was divorced, so they certainly need no special declaration about how the גט was written and signed. The גמרא will next ask what this ruling shows about the reason for the declaration.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; introduces a source as proof
Asked him
A country overseas
He divorced her
They are believed

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא is not saying that two people bringing a גט need nothing at all. He is saying they are believed as two witnesses, so the special declaration a single שליח makes is not needed for them.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דִּבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל מֵרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for שמואל asked רב הונא:
Two people who brought a גט from overseas,
must they say
'It was written in front of us and signed in front of us'
or don't they need to?
He said to him: They don't need to.
After all, if they said 'He divorced her in front of us,'
wouldn't they be believed?!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דִּבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל מֵרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the side discussion about rare cases, the גמרא brings a new source about the reason for the declaration
steps.raayaObject: The reason the Rabbis required the declaration (the dispute that רבה's view is part of)
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's question to רב הונא, and רב הונא's answer that two people bringing a גט do not need the declaration because two are believed as witnesses

steps.title: רב הונא's ruling fits רבא but not רבה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's ruling works for רבא but seems to clash with רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבא it works out well; according to רבה it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks רב הונא's ruling against the two reasons for the declaration. It finds that the ruling fits רבא but is a problem for רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the declaration exists because there are no witnesses to confirm the signatures. Two bringers can confirm the signatures themselves, so no declaration is needed. For רבה, the declaration exists because people overseas were not experts in writing a גט לשמה, and having two bringers does not solve that worry.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well; it fits
It is difficult; a problem
The אמורא who says the declaration is about לשמה
The אמורא who says the declaration is about confirming signatures (קיום)

steps.confusionAlert: רבה and רבא look almost the same in Hebrew. רבה (with a ה) is the one who focuses on לשמה. רבא (with an א) is the one who focuses on confirming the signatures.

phrases.english: According to Rava, it works out well,
phrases.notes: For רבא the point is confirming the signatures, and two bringers can do that themselves.

phrases.english: according to Rabba, it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the ראיה from רב הונא (step 13) against the dispute between רבה and רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reason for the declaration (worry about לשמה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two bringers solve the problem of confirming signatures, but they do not solve a לשמה problem. So why would רבה exempt them?

steps.title: The case is after they learned the laws
steps.stepSummary: For רבה, רב הונא's ruling is about a time after people overseas had learned the laws of לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? After they had learned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבה. It says רב הונא is talking about a time when people overseas already knew how to write a גט לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once people overseas know the laws of לשמה, רבה's worry is gone. All that is left is confirming the signatures, and two bringers can do that. So רב הונא's ruling fits רבה as well.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (The גמרא is narrowing the case.)
After they learned the law
Written for the sake of this specific woman

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
After they had learned.
phrases.notes: He means after the people overseas learned that a גט must be written for this woman's sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 14 for רבה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a specific time period
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא's ruling seemed to apply even when there is still a worry about לשמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling applies after people learned the laws, so only confirming the signatures matters, and two bringers can do that.

steps.title: Then even one bringer should be exempt
steps.stepSummary: If people have already learned the laws, even a single bringer should not need the declaration.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, one person should also not need it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If the people overseas already know the laws, why should even one bringer have to make the declaration?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's whole reason for the declaration was that people did not know the laws of לשמה. Once they do know, that reason seems to fall away for one bringer too. Yet one bringer still has to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
One person too

phrases.english: If so, one should also not need it!
phrases.notes: This means one person bringing the גט should also be free from saying the declaration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ruling is from after they learned the laws.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבה's reason is gone, then a single bringer should also be exempt, but he is not.

steps.title: A decree in case things go back to how they were
steps.stepSummary: One bringer must still say it because of a גזירה, in case people forget the laws again.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, in case the matter goes back to its bad state.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Rabbis kept the declaration for one bringer as a safeguard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though people know the laws now, they might forget them later. So the Rabbis made a גזירה that a single bringer must keep saying the declaration. The reason is not today's situation but the risk of slipping back.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
In case the matter goes back to its broken state

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest the matter return to its corrupt state.
phrases.notes: Literally, 'to its ruin.' He means people might forget the laws of לשמה again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once people know the laws, no one should need the declaration.
steps.terutzMaskana: One bringer still says it because of a decree in case people forget the laws again.

steps.title: Then two bringers should also need it
steps.stepSummary: If there is a decree, it should also cover two bringers.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, two people should also need it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the decree back around. If the Rabbis worried things might go back to how they were, that worry should apply to two bringers as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry that people might forget the laws of לשמה has nothing to do with how many people bring the גט. So the decree should apply to two bringers too, which goes against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Two people

phrases.english: If so, two should also need it!
phrases.notes: This means that because of the same decree, two bringers should also have to say the declaration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the decree answer from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decree that keeps the declaration in place.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The decree's worry applies the same way to two bringers, so רב הונא's exemption should not hold.

steps.title: Two bringers is a rare case
steps.stepSummary: Two people bringing a גט is rare, and the Rabbis do not make decrees for rare cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two people bringing a גט is uncommon, and the Rabbis did not decree about an uncommon case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the decree only covers the usual case, which is one bringer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט is usually sent with one messenger, and two messengers is unusual. The Rabbis aim their decrees at what usually happens, so they left the rare case of two bringers alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that does not happen often
The Rabbis did not make a decree about it
Who bring

steps.whyThisMatters: This uses again the general rule from step 8, that the Rabbis do not decree for rare cases. The next step tests that rule, just as step 9 did.

phrases.english: Two people who bring a bill of divorce,
is an uncommon matter;
and an uncommon matter,
the Sages did not decree about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּי תְרֵי דְּמַיְיתוּ גִּיטָּא, מִילְּתָא דְלָא שְׁכִיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general rule about the reach of rabbinic decrees
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree should cover every bringer, including two.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree covers only the common case. Two bringers is rare, so they are exempt.

steps.title: A woman bringing her own גט is also rare
steps.stepSummary: A woman bringing her own גט is rare, yet the משנה makes her say the declaration.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a woman bringing her own גט is uncommon too, and we learned: the woman herself may bring her גט, as long as she herself says 'it was written in my presence and signed in my presence'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule from the last step. It points to a rare case where the Rabbis did require the declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Rabbis never decree for rare cases, a woman bringing her own גט should be exempt. But the משנה clearly makes her say it, so the rule seems to be broken.

keyTerms.meaning: But look; introduces a challenge
And we learned (in a משנה)
As long as; on condition that
It was written in my presence and signed in my presence

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same challenge and answer you saw in steps 9 and 10. The גמרא repeats it here because the same rule about rare cases came up again.

phrases.english: But a woman is an uncommon case,
and we learned: The woman herself may bring her bill of divorce,
provided that she herself must say,
"It was written in my presence and signed in my presence"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule from step 19 that the Rabbis do not decree for rare cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the Rabbis do not decree for uncommon cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A woman bringing her own גט is uncommon, yet the משנה requires her to say the declaration.

steps.title: So that all kinds of agency follow one rule
steps.stepSummary: The woman says the declaration so that every kind of שליחות follows the same rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that you will not make a difference between kinds of agency.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the woman's case is not a separate decree. It is part of keeping the agency rules the same for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman acts as an agent just like any other single messenger. The Rabbis did not want one law for a regular messenger and a different law for her. So she says it to keep things uniform, and the rule about rare cases still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: So that you will not make a difference
Agency; acting as a messenger

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's exemption for two bringers works for both רבה and רבא. For רבה, it applies after people learned the laws. One bringer still says the declaration because of a גזירה. Two bringers do not, because their case is rare. A woman says it so that all kinds of שליחות follow one rule.

phrases.english: So that you will not distinguish between kinds of agency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20 and saves the rule from step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Keeping the rules for all agents the same
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The woman's case breaks the rule that the Rabbis do not decree for rare cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her declaration comes from keeping all agency rules the same, not from a separate decree for a rare case.

steps.title: Then a husband should also have to say it
steps.stepSummary: If every kind of שליחות follows the same rule, a husband bringing his own גט should also make the declaration. Yet a ברייתא says he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a husband should have to say it too! So why does a ברייתא teach that a husband who brings his own גט does not need to say 'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer, that all kinds of שליחות follow one rule. It points to a ברייתא that excuses the husband from the declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said the woman makes the declaration so that the rule stays uniform. If uniformity matters that much, the husband who carries his own גט should be included too. The ברייתא says he is not, so the principle seems to have a gap.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if what you just said is true
The husband
It was taught in a ברייתא
He himself

phrases.english: If so, a husband too!
phrases.notes: He means a husband who carries his own גט overseas to his wife should also have to make the declaration.

phrases.english: Why then is it taught:
He himself who brought his bill of divorce
is not required to say
"It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, בַּעַל נָמֵי! אַלְּמָה תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the uniform-שליחות answer of step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that every kind of שליחות follows the same rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule is truly uniform, the husband should be included too, yet a ברייתא exempts him.

steps.title: A husband holding the גט will not challenge it
steps.stepSummary: The declaration exists so that the husband cannot later come and challenge the גט. A husband who brings it himself would never do that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did the Rabbis require the declaration? Because perhaps the husband will come, challenge the גט, and make it invalid. But here he is holding it in his own hand. Would he then challenge it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the husband is different. The whole worry behind the decree simply does not apply to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree protects against the husband later claiming the גט is fake. When the husband delivers it himself, he obviously stands behind it. So he is outside the purpose of the decree; this is not a break in the uniform rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenges, contests (the validity of the גט)
Makes it invalid
Holds it in his hand

phrases.english: What is the reason the Rabbis said
he must say "It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence"?

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא אָתֵי בַּעַל מְעַרְעַר וּפָסֵיל לֵיהּ;
phrases.english: Perhaps the husband will come, contest it, and invalidate it.
Now he is holding it in his own hand,
and he would contest it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case by the reason behind the decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The husband should be included under the uniform rule
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband is outside the reason for the decree, since he will not challenge a גט he delivered himself
steps.whatToRemember: The declaration guards against the husband challenging the גט later. A husband who delivers it himself creates no such worry.

steps.title: A source: the declaration was a leniency
steps.stepSummary: A תוספתא rules that without the declaration, the גט is valid only if its signatures are confirmed. It explains that the declaration was meant to make things easier for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone brings a גט from overseas and gives it to her without saying 'It was written and signed in my presence,' then if its signatures are confirmed it is valid, and if not it is invalid. So they did not require the declaration to be strict with her, but to be lenient with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a תוספתא to test the two reasons for the declaration that were given earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because confirming the signatures is enough, the declaration serves as a stand-in for confirmation. That spares the woman the work of having the signatures checked. The תוספתא itself says the declaration exists to help her, not to burden her.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: introduces a source as a proof
A country overseas
Its signatures were confirmed by others
To be lenient with her
To be strict with her

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who brings a bill of divorce from overseas
and gave it to her but did not say to her
"It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence",
if it is confirmed through its signatures, it is valid,
phrases.notes: Other people come and identify the witnesses' signatures.

phrases.english: and if not, it is invalid.
So they did not require him to say
"It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence"
to be strict with her,
but rather to be lenient with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַמֵּבִיא גֵּט מִמְּדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source to test the reasons given earlier for the declaration
steps.raayaObject: That the declaration is a leniency, standing in for confirming the signatures

steps.title: This fits רבא but is hard for רבה
steps.stepSummary: The תוספתא matches רבא, who links the declaration to confirming signatures. It is hard for רבה, who links it to the worry about לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבא this works well, but according to רבה it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out who the תוספתא helps and who it hurts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the declaration replaces confirming the signatures, so it is a leniency, exactly as the תוספתא says. For רבה, it protects against a גט not written לשמה, which is a strictness. Under רבה, a גט without the declaration should not be saved just because its signatures were confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well
It is difficult
The אמורא who links the declaration to לשמה
The אמורא who links the declaration to confirming signatures

phrases.english: According to Rava it works well,
according to Rabba it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the source in step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reason for the declaration (concern about לשמה)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תוספתא calls the declaration a leniency, which fits only the confirmation reason and not the לשמה reason.

steps.title: The case is after people learned the laws
steps.stepSummary: The תוספתא is talking about the time after people overseas had learned that a גט must be written לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? After they learned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה by limiting the תוספתא to a later time period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once people overseas knew the law of לשמה, רבה's worry no longer applied. The only thing left to settle was the signatures, so confirming them is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? This introduces a narrower reading of a source.
After they learned (the law of לשמה)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
After they learned.
phrases.notes: He means after people overseas learned that a גט must be written for this specific woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 on behalf of רבה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific time period
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תוספתא contradicts רבה's לשמה reason
steps.terutzMaskana: Once people knew the law of לשמה, only the signatures needed checking

steps.title: But we decreed in case people forget again
steps.stepSummary: Even after people learned, the Rabbis kept the requirement in case things fall apart again. So why is the declaration not required here?
steps.simpleTranslation: But you yourself said there is a decree in case the matter goes back to its broken state!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer using רבה's own earlier decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said the declaration stays in place even after people learned, in case they forget again. If so, the time period should not matter, and the declaration should still be required.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't you say?
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
In case the matter goes back to its broken state

phrases.english: But didn't you say:
There is a decree, lest the matter return to its corrupt state!
phrases.notes: This points back to the reason given earlier for keeping the declaration even after people learned the law.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמְרַתְּ: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יַחְזוֹר הַדָּבָר לְקִלְקוּלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 26
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The decree applies even after people learned, so the time period cannot excuse the missing declaration.

steps.title: The woman had already remarried
steps.stepSummary: The תוספתא is talking about a woman who had already married someone else. The Rabbis did not apply their decree against her in that situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: When she had already married.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the case again. The woman has already remarried, so the decree is not enforced against her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree is only a precaution. Here the real worry is gone, and the woman has already remarried, so the Rabbis did not use the decree to break up her marriage. Confirming the signatures is enough after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: When she had (already) married

phrases.english: When she had married.
phrases.notes: She had already married another man after getting this גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: Further narrowing of the case (after the fact)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree should invalidate the גט even here
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree is not enforced once she has already remarried

steps.title: Then the תוספתא's reason does not fit
steps.stepSummary: If the real reason is that she remarried, the תוספתא should not explain the ruling by saying the declaration was a leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, how can the תוספתא say they did not require the declaration to be strict with her but to be lenient with her?! The real reason is that she had married!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. The explanation the תוספתא gives does not match the reason just suggested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תוספתא openly says the declaration exists as a leniency. That wording points to רבא's reason, confirming signatures. Under the answer in step 28, the real reason for the ruling would be her remarriage, which the תוספתא never mentions. So the wording of the תוספתא is still a problem for רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is because she had married

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two reasons. 'Lenient with her' is the reason the תוספתא gives. 'Because she married' is only the גמרא's suggestion to save רבה, and the גמרא now points out that the two do not match.

phrases.english: If so,
is it that they did not require him to say
"It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence"
to be strict with her
but rather to be lenient with her?!
It is because she had married!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הֱוֵי לָא הוּצְרְכוּ לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 28 by pointing to the תוספתא's wording
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תוספתא explains its ruling with 'lenient with her,' but under step 28 the real reason would be her remarriage, which does not match the stated reason.
steps.whatToRemember: The challenge here is about wording: the תוספתא explains its ruling as a leniency, while the remarriage answer suggests a different reason. The next step explains how the two fit together for רבה.

steps.title: The leniency line answers someone who wants to remove her
steps.stepSummary: The תוספתא mentions that the declaration was meant as a leniency to answer anyone who would want to be strict and separate the remarried woman from her new husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the תוספתא means: If you would say we should be strict with her and take her away from her new husband, the answer is that the Rabbis did not require the agent to say 'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence' to make things harder for her. They required it to make things easier for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 29. It explains why the תוספתא says the declaration was a leniency even though her remarriage is the main reason for the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The remarriage is the reason the Rabbis do not apply their decree. The leniency line is an extra point that blocks a possible objection: someone might want to be strict and take her away from her new husband. Since the declaration was made to help women, it cannot be used to break up her new marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means, a way of explaining what the source is really saying
And if you would say, which brings up a possible objection
To be strict with her
To take her out, meaning to separate her from her new husband
To be lenient with her, to make things easier for her

steps.whatToRemember: The תוספתא's ruling rests on the fact that she already remarried. The leniency line just stops anyone from using the declaration to be strict and break up her new marriage.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא dropped the remarriage answer. The remarriage is still the reason. The leniency line is an extra point that answers someone who wants to be strict.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is explaining what the תוספתא really means by its leniency line.

phrases.english: And if you would say, let us be strict with her
and take her out
phrases.notes: He means taking her away from the new husband she already married.

phrases.english: the answer is that they did not require him to say
"It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence"
in order to be strict with her
but rather to be lenient with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: וְכִי תֵּימָא לְהַחֲמִיר עֲלַהּ וְלַפְּקַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 29 by explaining what the leniency line in the תוספתא is doing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: the leniency line answers a possible objection and is not the main reason for the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The leniency line seemed to be the reason for the ruling, which would clash with the remarriage explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The remarriage is the reason the decree does not apply. The leniency line only answers someone who wants to be strict and separate her from her new husband, since the declaration was made to help her.
